topics.label: Course Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, outlines the cancer lecture series, and sets out the key learning objectives on environmental cancer causes, carcinogenicity testing, and tumor initiation versus promotion.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Genetic Basis, Environmental Risk, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as a genetic and evolutionary disease, present the roulette wheel model of intrinsic and environmental mutational risk, examine the debate over bad luck versus exposure, and analyze global epidemiological variation.

topics.label: Infectious Agents and Viral Oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how biological pathogens drive malignancy, detailing specific oncogenic viruses, bacteria, and parasites, with an in-depth case study of Burkitt lymphoma, malaria co-infection, and Epstein-Barr virus.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens: DNA Adducts and Metabolic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which dietary, environmental, and physical carcinogens—including aflatoxin, UV radiation, benzo[a]pyrene, TCDD, and aromatic amines—undergo xenobiotic metabolic activation to induce DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Initiator-Promoter Cooperation, and Host Context
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish non-mutagenic tumor promoters from mutational initiators using asbestos, the Berenbaum two-stage model of TPA and PKC activation, host developmental timing, and a synthesis of carcinogenesis mechanisms.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the experimental, computational, and population-based tools used to identify and evaluate carcinogens, including mutational signature sequencing, epidemiological biobanks, in vivo rodent assays, and the in vitro Ames test.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture by framing carcinogenic exposure within everyday risk-benefit decision-making and summarizing the primary lecture themes.
